record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.context_brief: Almost Borel classification with metric entropy
record.original_question: Does an analogue of the stated almost-Borel classification remain true when one discards only sets of zero Lebesgue measure and uses metric entropy instead of topological entropy, at least in dimension 2?

evidence.quote: Question 1.15 (Buzzi). I conjecture that a similar statement also holds when discarding only sets of zero Lebesgue measure using metric entropy instead of topological entropy (see [36]), at least in dimension 2 where we have the recent result [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A Borel dynamical system is a pair $(X,T)$ where $X$ is a standard Borel space and $T:X\to X$ is a Borel automorphism. Two Borel systems $(X,T)$ and $(Y,S)$ are said to be almost Borel isomorphic modulo a class $\mathcal N$ of "negligible" invariant Borel sets if there exist invariant Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ with $X\setminus X_0,\,Y\setminus Y_0\in\mathcal N$ and a Borel bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$. For a Borel system, the topological entropy refers to the supremum of Kolmogorov–Sinai (metric) entropies $h_\mu(T)$ taken over all $T$-invariant Borel probability measures $\mu$, and the metric entropy refers to $h_\mu(T)$ for a specified invariant measure class.

There is a known almost Borel classification theorem for sufficiently regular (e.g.\ smooth) dynamical systems in which one discards sets that are universally null (negligible for every invariant probability measure) and the invariant under consideration is the topological entropy; this classification realizes such systems, up to almost Borel isomorphism, as universal models built from Bernoulli shifts of prescribed entropies.

Problem. Let $f:M\to M$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact smooth surface $M$ (so $\dim M=2$), and equip $M$ with its Lebesgue (smooth volume) measure class. Does there exist an almost Borel classification of such systems, analogous to the one described above, in which:
(i) the negligible class $\mathcal N$ consists only of invariant Borel sets of Lebesgue measure zero (rather than universally null sets), and
(ii) the entropy invariant used is the metric entropy with respect to invariant probability measures (rather than the topological entropy)?

Equivalently, can every $C^\infty$ surface diffeomorphism be classified, up to Borel isomorphism after removing an invariant Borel set of Lebesgue measure zero, by its collection of ergodic invariant measures together with their metric entropies, in the spirit of the existing almost Borel classification?
artifact.category_tag: almost Borel classification of smooth dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture by Buzzi. While recent work of Buzzi–Crovisier–Sarig provides strong ergodic and measure-theoretic results for $C^\infty$ surface diffeomorphisms (proving Viana's conjecture in dimension 2), no search result indicates that an almost Borel classification modulo Lebesgue-null sets using metric entropy has been established. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Jérôme Buzzi's research works
status_evidence.snippet: Buzzi–Crovisier–Sarig results classify smooth surface diffeomorphisms with nonzero entropy; no almost-Borel-mod-Lebesgue classification noted.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surface-diffeomorphism results exist, but the specific almost Borel classification with metric entropy modulo Lebesgue-null sets is not reported as proved.
